question: If $\begin{vmatrix}x+1&2\\3&x-1\end{vmatrix}=-6$, determine all possible values of $x$ and find the sum of their squares.
explanation:
Expansion of the determinant
Using $\begin{vmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc$, $$\begin{vmatrix}x+1&2\\3&x-1\end{vmatrix}=(x+1)(x-1)-6$$
Application of the given value
Therefore, $$x^2-1-6=-6$$
Solution of the resulting equation
Simplifying gives $$x^2=1$$ Hence, $$x=1\quad\text{or}\quad x=-1$$
Sum of the squares
The required sum is $$1^2+(-1)^2=1+1=2$$
Thus, the possible values of $x$ are $1$ and $-1$, and the sum of their squares is $2$.
